term: categorical action duty in the agency control
definition: A separately interpreted predicate on actions, represented by GoalPractice.categoricalOught. It does not depend by definition on what an agent values, performs or successfully produces. Its intended contrast is with a conditional means-end requirement; it is not a theory of objectively binding morality or its justification.
note: The finite control alters this predicate while keeping the same valued goal, performed action and efficacy. This witnesses an absence of logical entailment only in the stated product profile; an ethical realist, constructivist or expressivist must defend a substantive bridge if an entailment is proposed. See docs/notes/transcendental-foundation-routes.md.
